cls: Pyrimidine synthesis inhibitor (dihydroorotate dehydrogenase inhibitor); immunomodulator
pharm: Disease-modifying therapy for relapsing multiple sclerosis
quick: 7 mg or 14 mg orally once daily
Avoid; do not breastfeed during treatment
Contraindicated in severe impairment; monitor ALT
ALT/bilirubin, CBC, BP, pregnancy status, TB screen
summary: Teriflunomide is an oral pyrimidine-synthesis (DHODH) inhibitor and the active metabolite of leflunomide, used as a disease-modifying therapy for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis. The dose is 7 mg or 14 mg once daily. It carries a BOXED WARNING for hepatotoxicity (including fatal liver failure) and major teratogenicity/embryofetal toxicity, requiring liver monitoring, pregnancy exclusion, effective contraception and an accelerated elimination procedure if pregnancy occurs or rapid clearance is needed. Other risks include myelosuppression, hypertension, infection and peripheral neuropathy.
indications: Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis in adults, including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease and active secondary progressive disease

dosage.d: 7 mg or 14 mg orally once daily
dosage.n: No loading dose; with or without food

dosage.d: Cholestyramine 8 g three times daily for 11 days, or activated charcoal 50 g twice daily for 11 days
dosage.n: Verify plasma level <0.02 mg/L on two tests >=14 days apart

admin: Swallow tablets whole; take once daily with or without food
Obtain baseline ALT, bilirubin, CBC, blood pressure and pregnancy test before starting
Screen for latent tuberculosis before initiation
Counsel on contraception (men and women) due to teratogenicity
Use the accelerated elimination procedure if rapid drug removal is required
moa: Teriflunomide selectively and reversibly inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH), a mitochondrial enzyme required for de novo pyrimidine synthesis. This reduces proliferation of rapidly dividing, activated T and B lymphocytes that depend on de novo synthesis, lowering the number of activated immune cells available to cause CNS inflammation in multiple sclerosis, while resting cells using the salvage pathway are relatively spared.

absolute: Pregnancy and women of childbearing potential not using reliable contraception
Known hypersensitivity to teriflunomide or leflunomide
Significant bone marrow impairment or severe uncontrolled cytopenia
relative: Pre-existing liver disease or alcohol use
monitor: ALT and bilirubin (baseline and at least monthly for 6 months)
CBC within 6 months before starting and as indicated

preg: Contraindicated (boxed warning). Teriflunomide is teratogenic and embryolethal in animals. Exclude pregnancy before starting, ensure effective contraception, and if pregnancy occurs stop the drug and perform the accelerated elimination procedure, targeting plasma levels <0.02 mg/L.
lact: Teriflunomide may be excreted in breast milk; breastfeeding is contraindicated during treatment.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in mild, moderate or severe renal impairment. Caution applies if undergoing dialysis (teriflunomide is highly protein bound and not appreciably dialysed).
hepatic: Hepatotoxicity is a boxed warning, including rare fatal liver failure. Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment. Obtain transaminase and bilirubin within 6 months before starting, monitor ALT at least monthly for 6 months, and discontinue with accelerated elimination if ALT rises >3x ULN.

major: Leflunomide - do not co-administer (teriflunomide is its active metabolite)
Other hepatotoxic drugs - increased risk of severe liver injury
Live vaccines - avoid due to immunomodulation and long half-life
moderate: Strong CYP/transporter substrates: rosuvastatin (limit dose), oral contraceptives (increased ethinylestradiol exposure)
BCRP and OAT3 substrates (e.g. methotrexate, repaglinide, paclitaxel) - increased exposure
minor: CYP1A2 substrates (caffeine, theophylline) - reduced exposure (teriflunomide is a mild inducer)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise ALT/AST/bilirubin, lower WBC/platelets, and reduce INR on warfarin.

serious: Severe hepatotoxicity, including fatal liver failure
Serious or opportunistic infections (including TB reactivation)
Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis / DRESS

monitoring: ALT and bilirubin at baseline then at least monthly for the first 6 months
CBC within 6 months before starting and as clinically indicated
Screen for latent TB before treatment; watch for infection and neuropathy
counsel: Use reliable contraception - this drug can seriously harm an unborn baby; tell your doctor at once if pregnancy is possible or occurs
Have regular blood tests to check your liver and blood counts
Stop and contact your doctor for yellowing of the skin/eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, fever, or unusual bruising/bleeding
Tell your doctor about any new numbness/tingling, persistent cough or breathlessness
An elimination procedure with cholestyramine or charcoal can quickly remove the drug if needed
pk: Steady state reached slowly (median ~3-4 months) due to long half-life
Persists for weeks to months; accelerated elimination needed for rapid removal
pearls: BOXED WARNING: hepatotoxicity (including fatal liver failure) and embryofetal toxicity - liver monitoring and pregnancy prevention are mandatory
Active metabolite of leflunomide - do not use the two together; extrapolate toxicity experience
Very long half-life (~2-3 weeks) and enterohepatic recycling: use cholestyramine/charcoal for accelerated elimination if pregnancy or severe toxicity occurs
Confirm plasma level <0.02 mg/L on two tests >=14 days apart after the elimination procedure
Screen for TB and avoid live vaccines during and after treatment
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost the next scheduled dose, skip it and resume the usual once-daily schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: No specific antidote for toxicity beyond drug removal. In overdose or severe toxicity, give cholestyramine or activated charcoal to accelerate elimination, and provide supportive care with monitoring of liver function and blood counts. Teriflunomide is not effectively removed by haemodialysis.
